subject: ss-plastic-surgery
title: Facial Palsy: House-Brackmann, Nerve Transfers and Gracilis Muscle

steps.say: Facial nerve injury is robbing the face of expression, eye closure, and oral competence all at once. The House-Brackmann scale is grading function from grade one with normal symmetry down to grade six with total paralysis and no tone. The bank figure is contrasting peripheral palsy affecting the whole hemiface with a central lesion sparing the forehead.
steps.tx: The **House-Brackmann** system grades **facial nerve function** from **Grade I** normal symmetry to **Grade VI** total paralysis without **tone**. Peripheral lesions denervate the whole hemiface including the forehead, while central lesions spare the upper face. Grading is guiding every **reconstruction** decision that follows.

vis.alt: Peripheral Bell palsy affecting the whole hemiface including forehead beside a central lesion sparing the forehead.
vis.caption: Peripheral versus central facial palsy. Grades and timing are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: The exposed cornea is facing ulceration within hours when lagophthalmos prevents closure. Lubricating drops with nighttime moisture chambers are keeping the surface wet around the clock. An implanted upper eyelid weight is letting gravity pull the lid closed with every blink.
steps.tx: **Corneal protection** in **lagophthalmos** is the paramount immediate priority. **Lubricating drops** with ointment and nighttime **moisture chambers** keep the surface wet, while upper eyelid **platinum or gold weight** implantation lets gravity close the lid. No **reconstruction** proceeds before the eye is safe.

steps.say: A sharply divided nerve is losing motor endplates with every passing hour after injury. Direct epineurial suture is joining the stumps within seventy two hours when they meet without tension. Longer gaps are receiving cable grafts of sural or great auricular nerve to bridge the defect.
steps.tx: Acute **facial nerve transection** within **72 hours** takes primary direct **epineurial end-to-end suture** for tension-free stump coaptation. Defects that cannot meet need **cable grafting** with **sural nerve** or **great auricular nerve** segments. Speed is deciding whether the native **mimetic muscles** survive the injury.

rows: Sural or great auricular cable graft

steps.say: Borrowed motor nerves are driving the old muscles while the motor endplates stay alive. The masseteric nerve from the third trigeminal division is powering a bite-driven smile within eighteen to twenty four months of denervation. The hypoglossal twelfth nerve is offering a stronger but less selective alternative drive.
steps.tx: While **mimetic muscles** stay viable under **18 to 24 months**, **masseteric nerve** transfer from motor V3 or **hypoglossal nerve (XII)** transfer restores a strong voluntary smile. Biting drives the **masseteric** smile, while tongue movement drives the **hypoglossal** one. Viable **endplates** are the entry ticket.

steps.say: Dead motor endplates are never waking up no matter which donor nerve is offered. Beyond two years the native muscles are becoming fibrotic cords that no transfer can revive. A transplanted gracilis with its own blood supply is replacing the whole contractile unit at this stage.
steps.tx: **Irreversible muscle atrophy** beyond **2 years** needs functional **free muscle transfer**. Microvascular **gracilis muscle transfer** is the global gold standard, arriving with its own **blood supply** and obturator nerve for coaptation. No **nerve transfer** works once the **endplates** are gone.

steps.say: A smile driven only by biting is looking voluntary rather than emotional in conversation. A sural nerve passed across the face is linking healthy buccal branches to the paralysed side for spontaneity. Axons are crossing the graft over nine to twelve months before the emotional smile appears.
steps.tx: **Cross-face nerve graft (CFNG)** with **sural nerve** coapted to healthy contralateral **buccal branches** gives a **spontaneous smile** driven by genuine emotion. **Axonal crossing** needs **9 to 12 months** before any movement appears on the reconstructed side. The healthy side is driving the reconstructed side during genuine emotion.

rows: Nine to twelve months for crossing

steps.say: Patients are wanting power now and spontaneity later from a single operation. Dual wiring is joining the transplanted gracilis to the masseteric nerve for immediate bite-driven movement. A cross-face graft is adding the emotional channel that matures months afterwards.
steps.tx: **Dual-innervation gracilis** transfer combines **masseteric nerve** power for immediate bite-driven movement with **CFNG** input for long-term emotional **spontaneity**. Patients bite to smile early, then the healthy side drives genuine emotion. Two **drives** mature on different timelines inside one transplanted muscle.

steps.say: Some patients are refusing long microsurgery or have no dynamic options left at all. Fascia lata strips are suspending the drooping oral commissure to restore resting symmetry. Acellular dermal matrix slings are stenting the collapsing nasal ala while holding the mouth corner up.
steps.tx: **Static reanimation** uses a **fascia lata sling** or **acellular dermal matrix slings** to suspend the drooping **oral commissure** and stent collapsing **nasal ala**. Resting **symmetry** returns without movement. Static slings suit patients refusing long surgery or lacking any **dynamic** option for smile restoration.
